How Color Flip’s palette cycle works

The current Color Flip palette rotates Coral, Teal, Gold, and Violet; learn how manual cycling, Color cycle mode, and the ten-target trail differ.

By NoCharge·Reviewed by NoCharge·Published August 15, 2026·Updated November 24, 2026·2 min read
Try the detail in a live board.

Pick a color. Step carefully. Take your time.

Play Color FlipBrowse all Articles

Bottom line: In current Color Flip, “cycle” refers to rotating the active swatch through Coral, Teal, Gold, and Violet. It is not a sequence of adjacent tiles or a separate turn-based board.

The four swatches

The palette order is Coral, Teal, Gold, Violet, then back to Coral. The target trail is shown separately: ten numbered positions, each with a named color. The current starting trail is deterministic and is restored by Reset to seeded start.

Three ways the active swatch can change

  • In Trail session, choose any named swatch for the current target. By default, the active swatch stays selected after you submit.
  • Use Cycle color to advance the active swatch manually through the four-color palette before submitting.
  • Choose Color cycle mode to advance the active swatch automatically after each submitted answer. The optional Rotate palette setting can also rotate it in Trail session.

The game compares the active swatch with the next target only when you activate Lock color and continue. A match adds one point; a miss leaves the score unchanged and does not end the session.

What stays visible

The current target is named in text and shown as a swatch. The trail shows which position is active and which ones are complete, and the scoreline reports matches. The session ends after ten submitted colors: ten matches is a win, and a lower completed total is a draw.

There is no timer, adjacent-tile movement, keyboard arrow route, saved best, or account record in this version. The buttons are standard controls and can be operated with the keyboard through focus and activation.
